title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with synthetic video. A generated clip presented a well known financial figure as the face of an investment offer, and the person who saw it treated the figure's apparent endorsement as the reason to trust the offer. The false claim was not made by a model in conversation but by a fabricated recording, which is harder for a viewer to interrogate because there is no exchange in which to ask questions.

The impersonation sat at the top of the funnel, in the advertisement itself. Everything after it, the WhatsApp contact, the help opening accounts, the remote access to the victim's computer, depended on the trust that the video had already created. Catching it would have required confirming that the person shown had actually made the endorsement, and checking whether the investment was authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, which is the check the PSNI advised. The reporting does not establish what checks, if any, were applied to the advertisement before it ran.

The celebrity is not named, and no arrest, charge or recovery of the funds is reported. The identity of the people behind the scam is not established, and the loss described is the victim's account as recorded by police rather than a finding by a court.

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in the Ards and North Down area lost £250,000 in an investment scam. Police Service of Northern Ireland said the victim saw an AI generated video that seemed to feature a well known financial figure. The ad promised an investment with large returns. After a small initial investment, fraudsters contacted the victim on WhatsApp and pushed for more payments. They helped create multiple online accounts and got remote access to the victim's computer, saying they were assisting with the investment.

Police described the fraud as advanced and large. The scammers built trust, urged the victim to borrow money, and moved funds to accounts they controlled. The PSNI did not name the celebrity. BBC News NI has seen similar scams using financial experts. Police advised people to verify who they deal with, check Financial Conduct Authority authorisation where relevant, and pause to check financial activity. Superintendent Joanne Gibson also urged families to discuss fraud with relatives.
title_en: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity
